title: Spectral Gap-Driven Coarsening for Dynamic Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks face a scalability bottleneck because they aggregate information over both graph topology and time, creating high computational demands.

gap.claim: Graph coarsening has reduced costs for static graph neural networks, but its potential in dynamic graph settings remains largely unexplored.

narrative_sequence.summary: DGNNs have a scalability bottleneck caused by computational demands across structural and temporal aggregation.
Coarsening has helped static graph neural networks, but remains underused in dynamic settings.
Applying coarsening dynamically is difficult because DGNN architectures aggregate across structural and temporal dimensions in different ways.

source_observation.claim: Dynamic graph models incur costs from jointly processing topology and temporal evolution.

interpretation.claim: Efficiency methods for dynamic graph models may need to account for both structural and temporal computation.

application.claim: When designing scalable dynamic graph systems, evaluate reductions in both graph-structural and temporal processing.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish that one efficiency strategy will generalize across all DGNN architectures.

unknowns: The supplied units do not describe the proposed coarsening method.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, or theoretical guarantees are provided.
The supplied units do not establish an explicit novel contribution.
